{{short description|Belgian mathematical physicist}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=September 2025}}
'''Bruno Leo Zulma Nachtergaele''' (24 June 1962 in [[Oudenaarde]])<ref>biographical information from ''American Men and Women of Science'', Thomson Gale 2004</ref> is a Belgian [[mathematical physicist]].

Nachtergaele studied physics with a [[Licentiate (degree)|licentiate degree]] in 1984 from the [[Katholieke Universiteit Leuven]]. There, he was awarded, in 1987, a doctorate in theoretical physics under André Verbeure with a dissertation ''Exacte resultaten voor het spin-Boson model'' (Exact results for the spin boson model), written in Dutch.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=59530|title=Bruno Leo Zulma Nachtergaele}}</ref> From 1989 to 1990 Nachtergaele was an instructor at the [[University of Chile]]. At [[Princeton University]], where he worked with [[Elliott Lieb]], Nachtergaele was from 1991 to 1993 an instructor and from 1993 to 1996 an assistant professor of physics. At the [[University of California, Davis]], he was from 1996 to 2000 an associate professor and has since 2000 been a full professor of mathematics. From 2007 to 2010, he was the chair of the Mathematics Department of the University of California, Davis.

His research concerns the mathematical physics of [[Statistical mechanics|equilibrium and nonequilibrium statistical mechanics]], [[quantum spin]] systems, and [[quantum information]].

He was elected in 2012 a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] and in 2007 a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]. In 2002 in [[Beijing]] he was an Invited Speaker, with [[Horng-Tzer Yau]], at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] with talk ''Derivation of the Euler equations from many-body quantum mechanics''.<ref>{{cite book|author=Nachtergaele, Bruno|author2=Yau, Horng-Tzer|chapter=Derivation of the Euler equations from many-body quantum mechanics|title=Proceedings of the ICM, Beijing 2002|year=2002|volume=3|pages=467–476|arxiv=math-ph/0210036}}</ref>

He was co-editor of 2 volumes of selecta of Elliott Lieb.

==Selected publications==
* with John Hunter: [https://books.google.com/books?id=VX9IDQAAQBAJ ''Applied Analysis''], World Scientific 2001
* with Mark Fannes & André Verbeure: ''The equilibrium states of the spin-boson model'', Comm. Math. Phys., 114, 1988, 537–548, 1988, [http://projecteuclid.org/DPubS?service=UI&version=1.0&verb=Display&handle=euclid.cmp/1104160777 Project Euclid]
* with Mark Fannes & Reinhard Werner: ''Finitely Correlated States on Quantum Spin Chains'', Comm. Math. Phys. 144, 1992, 443–490, [http://projecteuclid.org/DPubS?service=UI&version=1.0&verb=Display&handle=euclid.cmp/1104249404 Project Euclid]
* with [[Michael Aizenman]]: ''Geometric Aspects of Quantum Spin States'', Commun. Math. Phys., 164, 1994, 17–63, [https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9310009 Arxiv]
* with Elliott Lieb: The Stability of the Peierls Instability for Ring-Shaped Molecules, Phys. Rev. B, 51, 1995, 4777–4791, [https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9410100 Arxiv]
* with Horng-Tzer Yau: '' Derivation of the Euler Equations from Quantum Dynamics '', Commun. Math. Phys., 243, 2003, 485–540, [https://arxiv.org/abs/math-ph/0209027 Arxiv]
* wit Robert Sims: [https://arxiv.org/abs/math-ph/0512020 '' Recent progress in quantum spin systems ''], in J.T. Lewis '' Markov Processes and related fields '' 2007
* ''Quantum Spin Systems'', Encyclopedia of Mathematical Physics, Elsevier 2006, [https://arxiv.org/abs/math-ph/0409006 Arxiv]
